The sample this guide follows is [../samples/terminal_lifecycle.py].

Your first terminal asks for one terminal and watches it go live. This guide takes terminals you already have through the rest of their life — retire them, then ask for them again — and shows what you will see at each step.

What the states mean to you

State What is happening What you do
REQUESTED Accepted; waiting for room on capacity Submit the credential
PROVISIONING A host is preparing the terminal's folder Wait
LOGGING_IN The terminal is logging in to your broker Wait
ACTIVE Logged in, connected, ticks flowing Use it
OFFLINE The host running your terminal is down Nothing — see below
DRAINING You retired it; its host is stopping it Wait
RETIRED Stopped and removed from its host Nothing — it stays in your list as history
FAILED The broker refused the login, or it did not finish in time Read conditions, then submit the credential again, or retire it

state_since tells you when it entered the state, and state_expected_s how long that state usually takes — so you can tell "on time" from "longer than usual" without guessing.

When a terminal goes OFFLINE

OFFLINE means the machine your terminal runs on — its host — cannot run it right now. The terminal itself is fine, and so is your credential.

There is nothing for you to do. MFX notices within minutes and fixes it: the terminal comes back to ACTIVE on its own when its host reports again, or MFX moves it to another host in your farm if the host is not coming back. You do not retire it, you do not re-submit the credential, and you do not ask for a replacement — a new terminal would be a new id and a new login for a problem that is already being handled.

offline_reason says which of three things happened:

offline_reason What it means
power_off The host was turned off outside MFX
vm_missing The host's machine no longer exists, so the terminal is moved to another host
no_heartbeat The host has not reported for three minutes

While a terminal is OFFLINE, requests against it fail rather than wait. Retry them — that is the right response, and it is what the platform expects:

from mfx import is_usable

terminal = await client.terminals.get(terminal_id)
if not is_usable(terminal):
    # OFFLINE, or not live yet. Come back in a few seconds; do not re-create it.
    ...

is_usable() is true only for ACTIVE, so it stays right as the platform grows states. Checking state == "ACTIVE" yourself works today and will keep working — it is just one more place to remember.

Retiring is an intent, not a deletion

answer = await client.terminals.retire(terminal.id, idempotency_key="retire-42")
answer.state   # "DRAINING" — accepted, not finished

DELETE answers at once with the terminal DRAINING. It becomes RETIRED only when its host reports that the terminal has stopped, so poll until then. Three things worth knowing:

  • Retiring a terminal that is already DRAINING or RETIRED is not an error; you get it back as it is. Retry freely.
  • A terminal that is on its way to capacity (PROVISIONING, LOGGING_IN) answers 409 for now. Wait until it settles, then retire it.
  • A REQUESTED or FAILED terminal has nothing running, so it is RETIRED immediately.

A DRAINING terminal still holds its broker session. The session ends only when the terminal reads RETIRED, usually seconds later. If your broker's server allows only so many sessions on one login, wait for RETIRED before you start another terminal on that login, or the new one is refused because the login's sessions are all in use. The samples that retire a terminal poll every two seconds and stop waiting after two minutes, saying so, rather than hang.

Asking again

A retired terminal is never revived: you ask for a new one, and it gets a new id. Give it the instruments you want ticks for, in your broker's own names (EURUSD.sd, not EURUSD, if that is what your broker calls it) — MFX never renames an instrument on your behalf.

One Idempotency-Key makes one terminal. Send the same key with the same body and you get the original back; send it with a different body and you get a 409 that names the original.

What "live" means

ACTIVE plus three conditions reading ok:

Condition It is ok when
ProcessRunning the terminal process is up on its host
BrokerConnected the broker connection answered recently
TicksFresh a tick arrived for one of your instruments in the last few seconds, or their market is closed

A condition that is missing has not been observed yet; unknown means nobody could read it, which is different from failed.

A closed market is not a fault. When every instrument the terminal is judged on is outside its broker's trading sessions, TicksFresh stays ok and its reason reads market_closed: no tick is expected until the market opens, and the terminal is healthy. An ok with no reason means ticks are arriving. So at a weekend, read the reason before you conclude that prices are flowing.

A slow or quiet broker is said to be the broker's. A tick older than 15 seconds makes TicksFresh failed, whoever caused it: a stale price is a stale price, and the terminal's health is degraded. When your terminal is running and logged in and the only thing wrong is the broker's own feed, the condition says so in its reason and in attributed_to:

reason What it means
slow_feed this feed's own pace is slower than 15 seconds. Some feeds are simply slow: a crypto symbol at a weekend may quote less than once a minute. It reads slow_feed for as long as that is so, not once per gap
broker_quiet the last tick is well past the feed's own usual pace

Both carry attributed_to: "broker". MFX times each feed against its own measured pace, so a feed that is always slow is not reported as broken and one that stops is. Any other failed reason has attributed_to: null: it is not attributed, and you can ask us about it.

The terminal.condition_changed event carries the same attributed_to. It is sent when a condition's status changes, and also when a slow feed becomes a quiet broker or the reverse. A slow feed is one event when it becomes slow and one when its pace is back, not one for every late tick.

Run it

python samples/terminal_lifecycle.py all --terminal <terminal id> --key-id mfxk_... --private-key-file <your key file> --instruments EURUSD,XAUUSD

Your key needs the scopes term:read and term:write. Logins and passwords are typed at a prompt and go nowhere else. The script prints every change of state and condition with the seconds since it started, and ends with PASS or says what it was still waiting for.

The runnable sample: samples/terminal_lifecycle.py

Executed in CI against MFX Hub on every change to the knowledge base.

"""A terminal's whole life, twice: retire what you have, then ask for it again and watch it go live.

The runnable half of guides/a-terminals-whole-life.md. It does only what a customer can do — every call is the public, signed API through
the SDK — in three phases you can run together or one at a time:

    retire    the terminals you name with --terminal are retired - never any other; the script
              waits until each is RETIRED and writes what it was (farm, broker, server, instruments — no secret) to a plan file
    request   every terminal in the plan is asked for again, given its credential, and watched
              until it is ACTIVE with fresh ticks
    all       retire, pause until you press Enter, then request

    python samples/terminal_lifecycle.py all --terminal <terminal id> \\
        --key-id mfxk_... --private-key-file C:\\secure\\mfx-dev.key --instruments EURUSD,XAUUSD

Broker logins and passwords are typed at a prompt. They are never an argument, an environment
variable or a file, so they reach no shell history, no process list and no CI log — and the plan
file holds nothing you would mind losing.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import getpass
import json
import os
import time
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from mfx import MfxApiError, MfxClient, Secret, SigningKey

BASE_URL = "https://api.dev.mfxhub.com/v1"
PLAN = Path("terminal-lifecycle-plan.json")
POLL_S = 5
#: Generous on purpose: a cold host image pull and a first broker login are minutes, not seconds.
RETIRE_TIMEOUT_S = 15 * 60
ACTIVE_TIMEOUT_S = 20 * 60
LIVE = ("ProcessRunning", "BrokerConnected", "TicksFresh")

def private_key(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    """The API private key: the file named by --private-key-file, else MFX_PRIVATE_KEY."""
    if args.private_key_file is not None:
        return str(args.private_key_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
    key = os.environ.get("MFX_PRIVATE_KEY")
    if not key:
        raise SystemExit("give --private-key-file, or set MFX_PRIVATE_KEY")
    return key.strip()


def terminal_labels() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Labels for every terminal this sample asks for: MFX_TERMINAL_LABELS, a JSON object, when set.

    Optional. Labels are yours to sort and find terminals by; nothing here needs one.
    """
    labels = json.loads(os.environ.get("MFX_TERMINAL_LABELS") or "{}")
    return {str(key): str(value) for key, value in labels.items()}


def shown(terminal: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The terminal as plain data, so optional fields read the same whether or not they were sent."""
    data: dict[str, Any] = terminal.to_dict()
    return data


def conditions(terminal: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {name: c.get("status", "?") for name, c in shown(terminal).get("conditions", {}).items()}


def line(started: float, terminal: Any, note: str = "") -> None:
    data = shown(terminal)
    dots = " ".join(f"{name}={status}" for name, status in sorted(conditions(terminal).items()))
    elapsed = int(time.monotonic() - started)
    print(f"[{elapsed:>4}s] {data['broker']['label']:<14} {data['state']:<13} {dots} {note}".rstrip())


async def watch(client: MfxClient, ids: list[str], *, until: Any, timeout_s: int) -> list[Any]:
    """Poll until every terminal satisfies `until`, printing each change of state or condition."""
    started = time.monotonic()
    last: dict[str, Any] = {}
    done: dict[str, Any] = {}
    while len(done) < len(ids):
        if time.monotonic() - started > timeout_s:
            waiting = [i for i in ids if i not in done]
            raise SystemExit(f"FAILED: still waiting after {timeout_s}s for {waiting}")
        for terminal_id in ids:
            if terminal_id in done:
                continue
            terminal = await client.terminals.get(terminal_id)
            seen = (shown(terminal)["state"], tuple(sorted(conditions(terminal).items())))
            if last.get(terminal_id) != seen:
                last[terminal_id] = seen
                line(started, terminal)
            if until(terminal):
                done[terminal_id] = terminal
        await asyncio.sleep(POLL_S)
    return [done[i] for i in ids]


async def retire(client: MfxClient, names: list[str]) -> None:
    # Only the terminals named on the command line, and only those that are ACTIVE: a sample that
    # retired everything a tenant had would take its live terminals down with it.
    named = [await client.terminals.get(name) for name in names]
    active = [t for t in named if shown(t)["state"] == "ACTIVE"]
    if not active:
        raise SystemExit("None of the terminals named is ACTIVE, so there is nothing to retire.")
    plan = [
        {
            "was": str(t.id),
            "farm_id": shown(t)["farm"]["id"],
            "broker_id": shown(t)["broker"]["id"],
            "broker": shown(t)["broker"]["label"],
            "server_id": shown(t)["server"]["id"],
            "server": shown(t)["server"]["label"],
            "streaming": shown(t)["streaming"],
            "execution": shown(t)["execution"],
            "instruments": shown(t)["instruments"],
        }
        for t in active
    ]
    PLAN.write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"Retiring {len(active)} terminal(s); what they were is in {PLAN}")

    for terminal in active:
        # DELETE is an intent: the answer is DRAINING, and only the host's word makes it RETIRED.
        answer = await client.terminals.retire(terminal.id, idempotency_key=f"retire-{uuid.uuid4()}")
        print(f"  {shown(answer)['broker']['label']}: {shown(answer)['state']}")
    await watch(
        client,
        [str(t.id) for t in active],
        until=lambda t: shown(t)["state"] == "RETIRED",
        timeout_s=RETIRE_TIMEOUT_S,
    )
    print("PASS: every terminal drained on its host and is RETIRED.")


async def request(client: MfxClient, instruments: list[str]) -> None:
    if not PLAN.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"{PLAN} is missing: run `retire` first, or write it by hand.")
    plan = json.loads(PLAN.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    run = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]
    ids: list[str] = []
    for index, entry in enumerate(plan):
        wanted = entry["instruments"] or instruments
        # The key is fixed for this run: if the call is retried, the same terminal comes back.
        terminal = await client.terminals.create(
            farm_id=entry["farm_id"],
            broker_id=entry["broker_id"],
            server_id=entry["server_id"],
            streaming=entry["streaming"],
            execution=entry["execution"],
            instruments=wanted,
            labels={**terminal_labels(), "proof": run},
            idempotency_key=f"lifecycle-{run}-{index}",
        )
        print(f"{entry['broker']}: {terminal.id} {shown(terminal)['state']} watching {wanted}")

        login = int(input(f"  {entry['broker']} login number: ").strip())
        server = input(f"  {entry['broker']} server [{entry['server']}]: ").strip()
        await client.terminals.submit_credentials(
            terminal.id,
            login=login,
            password=Secret(getpass.getpass(f"  {entry['broker']} password: ")),
            server=server or entry["server"],
            idempotency_key=f"lifecycle-{run}-{index}-credential",
        )
        ids.append(str(terminal.id))

    def live(terminal: Any) -> bool:
        if shown(terminal)["state"] == "FAILED":
            raise SystemExit(f"FAILED: {shown(terminal)['broker']['label']} went FAILED")
        ok = conditions(terminal)
        return shown(terminal)["state"] == "ACTIVE" and all(ok.get(name) == "ok" for name in LIVE)

    await watch(client, ids, until=live, timeout_s=ACTIVE_TIMEOUT_S)
    print("PASS: every terminal is ACTIVE, connected to its broker, with fresh ticks.")


async def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("phase", choices=["retire", "request", "all"])
    parser.add_argument(
        "--terminal", action="append", default=[], help="a terminal to retire; give it once per terminal"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--key-id", default=os.environ.get("MFX_KEY_ID"), help="or MFX_KEY_ID")
    parser.add_argument("--private-key-file", type=Path, help="or the key itself in MFX_PRIVATE_KEY")
    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default=BASE_URL)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--instruments",
        default="",
        help="comma-separated, in the broker's own names; used for a terminal that had none",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    key = SigningKey(private_key(args))
    instruments = [name.strip() for name in args.instruments.split(",") if name.strip()]

    async with MfxClient(args.base_url, args.key_id, key) as client:
        try:
            if args.phase in ("retire", "all"):
                if not args.terminal:
                    raise SystemExit("name the terminals to retire: --terminal <id>, once per terminal")
                await retire(client, args.terminal)
            if args.phase == "all":
                # DECISION: no settle time is waited between retire and request. Each terminal
                # asked for again replaces one just RETIRED, so the login needs no session more
                # than it had, and RETIRED is the platform's word that the broker session is gone.
                # A pause guessed here would hide a session still counted wrong, and teach every
                # reader a number nobody measured.
                input("Terminals are retired. Press Enter when the host is ready for new ones... ")
            if args.phase in ("request", "all"):
                await request(client, instruments)
        except MfxApiError as refused:
            # The platform's own words: what was refused, why, and the request id to quote.
            raise SystemExit(f"REFUSED: {refused}") from None


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

comes back. terminal = await client.terminals.create( farm_id=entry["farm_id"], broker_id=entry["broker_id"], server_id=entry["server_id"], streaming=entry["streaming"], execution=entry["execution"], instruments=wanted, labels={**terminal_labels(), "proof": run}, idempotency_key=f"lifecycle-{run}-{index}", ) print(f"{entry['broker']}: {terminal.id} {shown(terminal)['state']} watching {wanted}") login = int(input(f" {entry['broker']} login number: ").strip()) server = input(f" {entry['broker']} server [{entry['server']}]: ").strip() await client.terminals.submit_credentials( terminal.id, login=login, password=Secret(getpass.getpass(f" {entry['broker']} password: ")), server=server or entry["server"], idempotency_key=f"lifecycle-{run}-{index}-credential", ) ids.append(str(terminal.id)) def live(terminal: Any) -> bool: if shown(terminal)["state"] == "FAILED": raise SystemExit(f"FAILED: {shown(terminal)['broker']['label']} went FAILED") ok = conditions(terminal) return shown(terminal)["state"] == "ACTIVE" and all(ok.get(name) == "ok" for name in LIVE) await watch(client, ids, until=live, timeout_s=ACTIVE_TIMEOUT_S) print("PASS: every terminal is ACTIVE, connected to its broker, with fresh ticks.") async def main() -> None: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0]) parser.add_argument("phase", choices=["retire", "request", "all"]) parser.add_argument( "--terminal", action="append", default=[], help="a terminal to retire; give it once per terminal" ) parser.add_argument("--key-id", default=os.environ.get("MFX_KEY_ID"), help="or MFX_KEY_ID") parser.add_argument("--private-key-file", type=Path, help="or the key itself in MFX_PRIVATE_KEY") parser.add_argument("--base-url", default=BASE_URL) parser.add_argument( "--instruments", default="", help="comma-separated, in the broker's own names; used for a terminal that had none", ) args = parser.parse_args() key = SigningKey(private_key(args)) instruments = [name.strip() for name in args.instruments.split(",") if name.strip()] async with MfxClient(args.base_url, args.key_id, key) as client: try: if args.phase in ("retire", "all"): if not args.terminal: raise SystemExit("name the terminals to retire: --terminal <id>, once per terminal") await retire(client, args.terminal) if args.phase == "all": # DECISION: no settle time is waited between retire and request. Each terminal # asked for again replaces one just RETIRED, so the login needs no session more # than it had, and RETIRED is the platform's word that the broker session is gone. # A pause guessed here would hide a session still counted wrong, and teach every # reader a number nobody measured. input("Terminals are retired. Press Enter when the host is ready for new ones... ") if args.phase in ("request", "all"): await request(client, instruments) except MfxApiError as refused: # The platform's own words: what was refused, why, and the request id to quote. raise SystemExit(f"REFUSED: {refused}") from None if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main())

documents.body_html:
Once a position is open you can protect it, take part of it off, and let the platform follow the price for you. This guide opens a small position, sets a stop loss and a take profit, closes half, puts a trailing stop on the rest, takes the trailing stop off again and closes the position. Use a demo account. The orders are real on whatever account you log in to.

The whole flow is one runnable file: samples/position_changes.py. Without --confirm it stops after the quote and opens nothing. Whatever happens, it closes the position it opened and retires its terminal before it ends.

Before you start

The same as your first order: an API key, your broker's and server's names, and a login and password for a demo account.

The steps

  1. A terminal, ACTIVE, a quote and the symbol's rules, as in pending orders.
  2. Buy twice the smallest volume, so that half of it can be closed on its own. The position's ticket is tickets.position on the result.
  3. Set a stop loss and a take profit with client.execution.modify_position(terminal_id, ticket, sl=..., tp=...). The sample puts each 2 % from the fill price, on the symbol's tick. A level too close to the price is refused with a reason that says so. Your broker sets the minimum distance (stops_level on the symbol).
  4. Close half with client.execution.close_position_partial(terminal_id, ticket, volume=...). The rest stays open under the same ticket. client.accounts.positions(terminal_id) shows its new volume once the account's next snapshot arrives, usually within seconds.
  5. Add a trailing stop with client.execution.set_trailing_stop(terminal_id, ticket, distance=...). The platform moves the stop loss up behind the best price the position reaches, never down. The position then carries trailing_stop, with its distance and state. Take it off with clear_trailing_stop. The stop loss stays where the trail left it.
  6. Close what is left with client.execution.close_position(terminal_id, ticket), and read the positions until the ticket is gone.
  7. Retire the terminal, and wait until it reads RETIRED before you start another terminal on the same login (see a terminal's whole life).

Every change is a command. Wait for each with client.execution.wait_for(command_id) and read state: SUCCEEDED happened, FAILED, EXPIRED and REJECTED did not, and UNKNOWN may have, so never send it again under a new key.

What you will see

farm MFX DEV, broker Pepperstone, server Pepperstone-Demo
REQUESTED
LOGGING_IN
terminal 06ada7be-1978-779d-8000-dc3528b97c84 is ACTIVE
EURUSD bid 1.12129 ask 1.12181, 1.2 s old
buy 0.02: SUCCEEDED
position 80123456 opened at 1.12183
stop loss 1.09939, take profit 1.14426: SUCCEEDED
close 0.01: SUCCEEDED
position 80123456 now holds 0.01
trailing stop 0.02243: SUCCEEDED
trailing stop 0.02243, active
trailing stop removed: SUCCEEDED
close: SUCCEEDED
position 80123456 is closed
terminal retired

This shows the shape of a run. Ids, tickets, prices and timings are illustrations, not figures to expect.

Where to go next

  • Sizing a position: from the money you will risk to a volume and a stop.
  • Following an account live: see each change arrive as it happens.
  • The execution reference: every position command and field.

The runnable sample: samples/position_changes.py

Executed in CI against MFX Hub on every change to the knowledge base.

"""A position from open to close, changed on the way: the runnable half of guides/changing-a-position.md.

It finds your farm, broker and server by name, asks for a terminal, logs it in, buys twice the
smallest volume, sets a stop loss and a take profit, closes half, puts a trailing stop on the rest,
takes the trailing stop off, closes the position, and retires the terminal. Use a **demo** account:
the orders are real on whatever account you log in to.

    MFX_KEY_ID=mfxk_... MFX_PRIVATE_KEY="$(cat my.key)" \\
    MFX_BROKER=Pepperstone MFX_SERVER=Pepperstone-Demo MFX_LOGIN=12345678 \\
    python samples/position_changes.py --symbol EURUSD --confirm

Without ``--confirm`` it stops after the quote and opens nothing. Whatever happens, it closes the
position it opened and retires the terminal before it ends, so a run leaves nothing behind. The
broker password is typed at a prompt: never an argument, an environment variable or a file.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import asyncio
import getpass
import json
import os
import time
import uuid
from collections.abc import Callable
from decimal import ROUND_FLOOR, Decimal
from typing import Any

import mfx
from mfx import ExecutionResult, MfxClient, NotFoundError, SigningKey

BASE_URL = os.environ.get("MFX_BASE_URL", "https://api.dev.mfxhub.com/v1")
#: How long to wait for a terminal you retired to read RETIRED. A drain takes seconds; this is
#: only the point at which the sample stops waiting and says so.
RETIRE_WAIT_S = 120
RETIRE_POLL_S = 2
#: How far the stop loss and take profit sit from the price: wide, so neither is hit while it runs.
AWAY = Decimal("0.02")
#: How long to wait for the positions list to show a change (it is a snapshot of the account).
LIST_WAIT_S = 30


async def wait_until_retired(
    client: MfxClient,
    terminal_id: uuid.UUID | str,
    *,
    wait_s: float = RETIRE_WAIT_S,
    poll_s: float = RETIRE_POLL_S,
) -> bool:
    """Wait until a terminal you retired reads RETIRED, or is gone. False if not within ``wait_s``.

    Retiring is accepted at once and the terminal reads DRAINING; it keeps its broker session until
    its host has stopped it and it reads RETIRED. On a login whose server allows only so many
    sessions, wait for RETIRED before you start another terminal on that login.
    """
    deadline = time.monotonic() + wait_s
    while True:
        try:
            terminal = await client.terminals.get(terminal_id)
        except NotFoundError:
            return True  # nothing is left to hold a session
        if terminal.state == "RETIRED":
            return True
        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            return False
        await asyncio.sleep(poll_s)


def terminal_labels() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Labels for every terminal this sample asks for: MFX_TERMINAL_LABELS, a JSON object, when set.

    Optional. Labels are yours to sort and find terminals by; nothing here needs one.
    """
    labels = json.loads(os.environ.get("MFX_TERMINAL_LABELS") or "{}")
    return {str(key): str(value) for key, value in labels.items()}


async def find_ids(client: MfxClient, broker: str, server: str) -> tuple[str, str, str, set[str]]:
    """The farm, broker and server ids for the names you know, and what the farm offers."""
    wanted = os.environ.get("MFX_FARM_ID")
    farm = None
    async for candidate in client.farms.list():
        offers = {str(usage) for usage in candidate.usages}
        if str(candidate.id) == wanted or (not wanted and "order_execution" in offers):
            farm = candidate
            break
    if farm is None:
        raise SystemExit("no farm on your plan executes orders; ask support which one to use")
    broker_row = None
    async for row in client.catalog.all_brokers():
        if broker.lower() in {row.code.lower(), row.display_name.lower()}:
            broker_row = row
            break
    if broker_row is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"no broker called {broker!r}; client.catalog.all_brokers() lists them")
    servers = await client.catalog.servers(broker_row.id)
    server_row = next((s for s in servers if s.server_name.lower() == server.lower()), None)
    if server_row is None or not server_row.enabled:
        names = ", ".join(s.server_name for s in servers if s.enabled)
        raise SystemExit(f"server {server!r} is not available; {broker_row.display_name} offers {names}")
    print(f"farm {farm.name}, broker {broker_row.display_name}, server {server_row.server_name}")
    return str(farm.id), str(broker_row.id), str(server_row.id), offers


def on_tick(price: Decimal, spec: Any) -> str:
    """A price the broker accepts: down onto the symbol's tick, written with its digits."""
    digits = int(spec.digits)
    tick = Decimal(str(getattr(spec, "tick_size", None) or getattr(spec, "point", None)
                       or Decimal(1).scaleb(-digits)))  # fmt: skip
    snapped = (price / tick).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR) * tick
    return format(snapped.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-digits)), "f")


async def final(client: MfxClient, result: ExecutionResult) -> ExecutionResult:
    """The command's final result. Execution never raises, so every step waits and reads state."""
    return await client.execution.wait_for(result.command_id) if result.command_id else result


def check(step: str, result: ExecutionResult) -> None:
    print(f"{step}: {result.state}")
    if str(result.state) != "SUCCEEDED":
        raise SystemExit(f"{step} did not succeed: {result.reason_text or result.detail}")


async def position(client: MfxClient, terminal_id: uuid.UUID | str, ticket: int) -> Any:
    """The position by its ticket, from the account's latest snapshot; None once it is closed."""
    rows = (await client.accounts.positions(terminal_id)).items
    return next((p for p in rows if p.ticket == ticket), None)


async def until(
    client: MfxClient, terminal_id: uuid.UUID | str, ticket: int, seen: Callable[[Any], Any], what: str
) -> Any:
    """Wait for the position to show a change: the list is read from a snapshot of the account."""
    for _ in range(LIST_WAIT_S):
        row = await position(client, terminal_id, ticket)
        if seen(row):
            return row
        await asyncio.sleep(1)
    raise SystemExit(f"position {ticket}: {what} not seen after {LIST_WAIT_S} s")



async def priced(
    client: MfxClient, broker_id: str, symbol: str, server_id: str
) -> tuple[Any, str | None]:
    """The symbol's quote, and the account type it was asked under. A server may list one symbol
    under several account types; a quote that names none is then refused as ambiguous, so it is
    asked again under each listing's account type until one answers."""
    try:
        return await client.catalog.quote(broker_id, symbol, server_id=server_id), None
    except mfx.MfxApiError as refused:
        if refused.code != "ambiguous_symbol":
            raise
        last = refused
    cursor = None
    while True:
        page = await client.catalog.symbols(broker_id, server_id=server_id, cursor=cursor, limit=200)
        for listed in (s for s in page.items if s.symbol == symbol and s.account_type):
            try:
                quote = await client.catalog.quote(broker_id, symbol, server_id=server_id,
                                                   account_type=listed.account_type)  # fmt: skip
            except mfx.MfxApiError as refused:
                last = refused
                continue
            return quote, listed.account_type
        cursor = page.next_cursor
        if not cursor:
            raise last

async def main(symbol: str, confirm: bool) -> None:
    run = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]  # one run, one set of idempotency keys: a retry repeats nothing
    mark = f"mfx-sample-{run}"  # on the order's comment, so this run finds its own position
    async with MfxClient(
        BASE_URL, os.environ["MFX_KEY_ID"], SigningKey(os.environ["MFX_PRIVATE_KEY"])
    ) as client:
        farm_id, broker_id, server_id, offers = await find_ids(
            client, os.environ["MFX_BROKER"], os.environ["MFX_SERVER"]
        )
        execution = client.execution

        # 1. A terminal for your account, as in your first order.
        terminal = await client.terminals.create(
            farm_id=farm_id,
            broker_id=broker_id,
            server_id=server_id,
            streaming="quote_streaming" in offers,
            execution="order_execution" in offers,
            instruments=[symbol],
            labels=terminal_labels(),
            idempotency_key=f"position-terminal-{run}",
        )
        try:
            await client.terminals.submit_credentials(
                terminal.id,
                login=int(os.environ["MFX_LOGIN"]),
                password=mfx.Secret(getpass.getpass("Broker password: ")),
                server=os.environ["MFX_SERVER"],
                idempotency_key=f"position-credential-{run}",
            )
            while not mfx.is_usable(terminal := await client.terminals.get(terminal.id)):
                if terminal.state in ("FAILED", "RETIRED"):
                    raise SystemExit(f"the terminal ended {terminal.state}: read its conditions")
                print(terminal.state)
                await asyncio.sleep(5)
            print(f"terminal {terminal.id} is ACTIVE")

            # 2. A quote and the symbol's rules.
            quote, account_type = await priced(client, broker_id, symbol, server_id)
            spec = await client.catalog.symbol(broker_id, symbol, server_id=server_id,
                                   account_type=account_type)
            print(f"{symbol} bid {quote.bid} ask {quote.ask}, {quote.age_s:.1f} s old")
            if not confirm:
                print("not opening a position: pass --confirm to open, change and close one")
                return

            # 3. Buy twice the smallest volume, so half of it can be closed on its own.
            half = Decimal(str(spec.volume_min))
            opened = await final(
                client,
                await execution.place_order(
                    terminal.id,
                    symbol=symbol,
                    side="buy",
                    volume=str(half * 2),
                    comment=mark,
                    idempotency_key=f"position-buy-{run}",
                ),
            )
            check(f"buy {half * 2}", opened)
            ticket = opened.tickets.position
            if ticket is None:
                raise SystemExit("the order filled but named no position")
            print(f"position {ticket} opened at {opened.exec_price}")

            # 4. A stop loss and a take profit, each 2 % from the price.
            price = Decimal(str(opened.exec_price or quote.ask))
            sl, tp = on_tick(price * (1 - AWAY), spec), on_tick(price * (1 + AWAY), spec)
            changed = await execution.modify_position(
                terminal.id, ticket, sl=sl, tp=tp, idempotency_key=f"position-sltp-{run}"
            )
            check(f"stop loss {sl}, take profit {tp}", await final(client, changed))

            # 5. Close half. The rest stays open under the same ticket.
            partial = await execution.close_position_partial(
                terminal.id, ticket, volume=str(half), idempotency_key=f"position-half-{run}"
            )
            check(f"close {half}", await final(client, partial))
            await until(
                client, terminal.id, ticket,
                lambda row: row is not None and Decimal(row.volume) == half, f"volume {half}",
            )  # fmt: skip
            print(f"position {ticket} now holds {half}")

            # 6. A trailing stop: the platform moves the stop loss up behind the best price.
            distance = on_tick(price * AWAY, spec)
            trail = await execution.set_trailing_stop(
                terminal.id, ticket, distance=distance, idempotency_key=f"position-trail-{run}"
            )
            check(f"trailing stop {distance}", await final(client, trail))
            row = await until(
                client, terminal.id, ticket,
                lambda row: row is not None and row.trailing_stop, "a trailing stop",
            )  # fmt: skip
            print(f"trailing stop {row.trailing_stop.distance}, {row.trailing_stop.state}")
            untrail = await execution.clear_trailing_stop(
                terminal.id, ticket, idempotency_key=f"position-untrail-{run}"
            )
            check("trailing stop removed", await final(client, untrail))

            # 7. Close what is left.
            closed = await execution.close_position(
                terminal.id, ticket, idempotency_key=f"position-close-{run}"
            )
            check("close", await final(client, closed))
            await until(client, terminal.id, ticket, lambda row: row is None, "the close")
            print(f"position {ticket} is closed")
        finally:
            # 8. Leave nothing behind: any position of this run still open (found by its comment,
            # so even one whose outcome was unknown) is closed, then the terminal is retired.
            try:
                rows = (await client.accounts.positions(terminal.id)).items if confirm else []
            except mfx.MfxError as exc:  # a terminal that never went live has nothing open
                print(f"could not read positions on the way out: {exc}")
                rows = []
            for left in rows:
                if left.comment == mark:
                    done = await final(
                        client,
                        await execution.close_position(
                            terminal.id,
                            left.ticket,
                            idempotency_key=f"position-cleanup-{left.ticket}-{run}",
                        ),
                    )
                    print(f"position {left.ticket} closed on the way out: {done.state}")
            await client.terminals.retire(terminal.id, idempotency_key=f"position-retire-{run}")
            if await wait_until_retired(client, terminal.id):
                print("terminal retired")
            else:
                print(f"not RETIRED after {RETIRE_WAIT_S} s: it may still hold its broker session")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("--symbol", default="EURUSD", help="the broker's own symbol name")
    parser.add_argument("--confirm", action="store_true", help="open the position (demo accounts)")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    asyncio.run(main(args.symbol, args.confirm))

""" labels = json.loads(os.environ.get("MFX_TERMINAL_LABELS") or "{}") return {str(key): str(value) for key, value in labels.items()} async def find_ids(client: MfxClient, broker: str, server: str) -> tuple[str, str, str, set[str]]: """The farm, broker and server ids for the names you know, and what the farm offers.""" wanted = os.environ.get("MFX_FARM_ID") farm = None async for candidate in client.farms.list(): offers = {str(usage) for usage in candidate.usages} if str(candidate.id) == wanted or (not wanted and "order_execution" in offers): farm = candidate break if farm is None: raise SystemExit("no farm on your plan executes orders; ask support which one to use") broker_row = None async for row in client.catalog.all_brokers(): if broker.lower() in {row.code.lower(), row.display_name.lower()}: broker_row = row break if broker_row is None: raise SystemExit(f"no broker called {broker!r}; client.catalog.all_brokers() lists them") servers = await client.catalog.servers(broker_row.id) server_row = next((s for s in servers if s.server_name.lower() == server.lower()), None) if server_row is None or not server_row.enabled: names = ", ".join(s.server_name for s in servers if s.enabled) raise SystemExit(f"server {server!r} is not available; {broker_row.display_name} offers {names}") print(f"farm {farm.name}, broker {broker_row.display_name}, server {server_row.server_name}") return str(farm.id), str(broker_row.id), str(server_row.id), offers def on_tick(price: Decimal, spec: Any) -> str: """A price the broker accepts: down onto the symbol's tick, written with its digits.""" digits = int(spec.digits) tick = Decimal(str(getattr(spec, "tick_size", None) or getattr(spec, "point", None) or Decimal(1).scaleb(-digits))) # fmt: skip snapped = (price / tick).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_FLOOR) * tick return format(snapped.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-digits)), "f") async def final(client: MfxClient, result: ExecutionResult) -> ExecutionResult: """The command's final result. Execution never raises, so every step waits and reads state.""" return await client.execution.wait_for(result.command_id) if result.command_id else result def check(step: str, result: ExecutionResult) -> None: print(f"{step}: {result.state}") if str(result.state) != "SUCCEEDED": raise SystemExit(f"{step} did not succeed: {result.reason_text or result.detail}") async def position(client: MfxClient, terminal_id: uuid.UUID | str, ticket: int) -> Any: """The position by its ticket, from the account's latest snapshot; None once it is closed.""" rows = (await client.accounts.positions(terminal_id)).items return next((p for p in rows if p.ticket == ticket), None) async def until( client: MfxClient, terminal_id: uuid.UUID | str, ticket: int, seen: Callable[[Any], Any], what: str ) -> Any: """Wait for the position to show a change: the list is read from a snapshot of the account.""" for _ in range(LIST_WAIT_S): row = await position(client, terminal_id, ticket) if seen(row): return row await asyncio.sleep(1) raise SystemExit(f"position {ticket}: {what} not seen after {LIST_WAIT_S} s") async def priced( client: MfxClient, broker_id: str, symbol: str, server_id: str ) -> tuple[Any, str | None]: """The symbol's quote, and the account type it was asked under. A server may list one symbol under several account types; a quote that names none is then refused as ambiguous, so it is asked again under each listing's account type until one answers.""" try: return await client.catalog.quote(broker_id, symbol, server_id=server_id), None except mfx.MfxApiError as refused: if refused.code != "ambiguous_symbol": raise last = refused cursor = None while True: page = await client.catalog.symbols(broker_id, server_id=server_id, cursor=cursor, limit=200) for listed in (s for s in page.items if s.symbol == symbol and s.account_type): try: quote = await client.catalog.quote(broker_id, symbol, server_id=server_id, account_type=listed.account_type) # fmt: skip except mfx.MfxApiError as refused: last = refused continue return quote, listed.account_type cursor = page.next_cursor if not cursor: raise last async def main(symbol: str, confirm: bool) -> None: run = uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] # one run, one set of idempotency keys: a retry repeats nothing mark = f"mfx-sample-{run}" # on the order's comment, so this run finds its own position async with MfxClient( BASE_URL, os.environ["MFX_KEY_ID"], SigningKey(os.environ["MFX_PRIVATE_KEY"]) ) as client: farm_id, broker_id, server_id, offers = await find_ids( client, os.environ["MFX_BROKER"], os.environ["MFX_SERVER"] ) execution = client.execution # 1. A terminal for your account, as in your first order. terminal = await client.terminals.create( farm_id=farm_id, broker_id=broker_id, server_id=server_id, streaming="quote_streaming" in offers, execution="order_execution" in offers, instruments=[symbol], labels=terminal_labels(), idempotency_key=f"position-terminal-{run}", ) try: await client.terminals.submit_credentials( terminal.id, login=int(os.environ["MFX_LOGIN"]), password=mfx.Secret(getpass.getpass("Broker password: ")), server=os.environ["MFX_SERVER"], idempotency_key=f"position-credential-{run}", ) while not mfx.is_usable(terminal := await client.terminals.get(terminal.id)): if terminal.state in ("FAILED", "RETIRED"): raise SystemExit(f"the terminal ended {terminal.state}: read its conditions") print(terminal.state) await asyncio.sleep(5) print(f"terminal {terminal.id} is ACTIVE") # 2. A quote and the symbol's rules. quote, account_type = await priced(client, broker_id, symbol, server_id) spec = await client.catalog.symbol(broker_id, symbol, server_id=server_id, account_type=account_type) print(f"{symbol} bid {quote.bid} ask {quote.ask}, {quote.age_s:.1f} s old") if not confirm: print("not opening a position: pass --confirm to open, change and close one") return # 3. Buy twice the smallest volume, so half of it can be closed on its own. half = Decimal(str(spec.volume_min)) opened = await final( client, await execution.place_order( terminal.id, symbol=symbol, side="buy", volume=str(half * 2), comment=mark, idempotency_key=f"position-buy-{run}", ), ) check(f"buy {half * 2}", opened) ticket = opened.tickets.position if ticket is None: raise SystemExit("the order filled but named no position") print(f"position {ticket} opened at {opened.exec_price}") # 4. A stop loss and a take profit, each 2 % from the price. price = Decimal(str(opened.exec_price or quote.ask)) sl, tp = on_tick(price * (1 - AWAY), spec), on_tick(price * (1 + AWAY), spec) changed = await execution.modify_position( terminal.id, ticket, sl=sl, tp=tp, idempotency_key=f"position-sltp-{run}" ) check(f"stop loss {sl}, take profit {tp}", await final(client, changed)) # 5. Close half. The rest stays open under the same ticket. partial = await execution.close_position_partial( terminal.id, ticket, volume=str(half), idempotency_key=f"position-half-{run}" ) check(f"close {half}", await final(client, partial)) await until( client, terminal.id, ticket, lambda row: row is not None and Decimal(row.volume) == half, f"volume {half}", ) # fmt: skip print(f"position {ticket} now holds {half}") # 6. A trailing stop: the platform moves the stop loss up behind the best price. distance = on_tick(price * AWAY, spec) trail = await execution.set_trailing_stop( terminal.id, ticket, distance=distance, idempotency_key=f"position-trail-{run}" ) check(f"trailing stop {distance}", await final(client, trail)) row = await until( client, terminal.id, ticket, lambda row: row is not None and row.trailing_stop, "a trailing stop", ) # fmt: skip print(f"trailing stop {row.trailing_stop.distance}, {row.trailing_stop.state}") untrail = await execution.clear_trailing_stop( terminal.id, ticket, idempotency_key=f"position-untrail-{run}" ) check("trailing stop removed", await final(client, untrail)) # 7. Close what is left. closed = await execution.close_position( terminal.id, ticket, idempotency_key=f"position-close-{run}" ) check("close", await final(client, closed)) await until(client, terminal.id, ticket, lambda row: row is None, "the close") print(f"position {ticket} is closed") finally: # 8. Leave nothing behind: any position of this run still open (found by its comment, # so even one whose outcome was unknown) is closed, then the terminal is retired. try: rows = (await client.accounts.positions(terminal.id)).items if confirm else [] except mfx.MfxError as exc: # a terminal that never went live has nothing open print(f"could not read positions on the way out: {exc}") rows = [] for left in rows: if left.comment == mark: done = await final( client, await execution.close_position( terminal.id, left.ticket, idempotency_key=f"position-cleanup-{left.ticket}-{run}", ), ) print(f"position {left.ticket} closed on the way out: {done.state}") await client.terminals.retire(terminal.id, idempotency_key=f"position-retire-{run}") if await wait_until_retired(client, terminal.id): print("terminal retired") else: print(f"not RETIRED after {RETIRE_WAIT_S} s: it may still hold its broker session") if __name__ == "__main__": parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0]) parser.add_argument("--symbol", default="EURUSD", help="the broker's own symbol name") parser.add_argument("--confirm", action="store_true", help="open the position (demo accounts)") args = parser.parse_args() asyncio.run(main(args.symbol, args.confirm))

documents.body_html:
Runs against the dev environment today, where every path below was run on 2 October 2026, and a change on a terminal with open positions on 3 October 2026. The sample it quotes is [../samples/change_password.py].

You changed your password at the broker, or the one you submitted was wrong and the terminal is FAILED. Either way the fix is the same call you used the first time: submit the credential again. You do not retire the terminal, and it keeps its id, its instruments and its history.

Submit it again

From the sample:

return await client.terminals.submit_credentials(
    terminal_id,
    login=login,
    password=password,
    server=server,
    idempotency_key=f"change-password-{uuid.uuid4()}",
)

takes_effect = field(answer, "takes_effect", "first_login")

The first submission for a terminal stores its credential. Every later one for the same login replaces the password. The answer tells you when the terminal will use it:

takes_effect The terminal was What happens
restart ACTIVE It is restarted now and logs in with the new password. Expect a short gap in ticks
retry_login FAILED It rejoins the login queue now. This is how you recover from a wrong password
next_login anything else Nothing is started. Its next login uses the new password
first_login new, with no credential yet The ordinary first submission

operation_id names the restart or retry so you can follow it. It is empty for next_login.

Open positions do not hold a password change back. An ACTIVE terminal is restarted even when the account has open positions, because a restart is the only way the new password is used. Your positions stay open at the broker while the terminal reconnects; expect a gap of a few seconds in ticks and account updates.

You can still get next_login for an ACTIVE or FAILED terminal. That means the restart or retry could not start right now, and not_applied_reason says why, using the same code the restart call would have answered:

not_applied_reason Means
operation_in_progress Another restart, rebuild or move is already running on this terminal
cooldown The terminal was restarted moments ago
tenant_rate or concurrency You have used your restarts for now
positions_open Your platform operator has switched on the confirmation for restarts with open positions

The new password is stored all the same. Restart the terminal when you are ready, or leave it: its next login uses the new password. not_applied_reason is empty in every other answer.

What is refused

  • A different login. The call answers 409 conflict with details.reason set to login_changed. Another login is another account, with its own positions and history, so it needs its own terminal: request a new one, and retire this one when you are done with it.
  • A terminal that is going. DRAINING and RETIRED answer 409 state_error.
  • A different server. The credential's server must be the terminal's own; anything else is a 400.

When the broker says no

If the broker refuses the login, the terminal becomes FAILED within a couple of minutes and its BrokerConnected condition reads failed with the reason login_refused. MFX Hub does not keep retrying a refused login, because repeated bad logins are how a broker locks an account. Nothing happens until you act:

  1. Check the login, the password and the server at your broker.
  2. Submit the credential again. The answer is retry_login and the terminal logs in.

A login that fails for another reason, such as a broker that did not answer in time, is different: MFX Hub tries it again by itself after 30 minutes, up to three times in a day. You can still submit the credential again, or ask for a retry, without waiting.

A broker gives the same answer for a wrong password as for an account that no longer exists, so MFX Hub only ever tells you that the login was refused. Demo accounts expire; if the password is right and the login is still refused, check that the account is still open.

An investor password

Submitting an investor (read-only) password turns order execution off for the terminal, and the answer says so in execution_disabled. Submitting a master password later does not turn it back on by itself.

More than one terminal on the login

Each terminal holds its own copy of the credential, so a password you changed at the broker has to be submitted to every terminal that uses the login. The answer counts what is left: same_login_terminals_stale is how many of your other terminals on the login were last given their password before this one. Submit to each until it reads 0. See Several terminals on one broker login.

Your password is never returned

The password travels once, over TLS, into the platform's vault. No API returns it, no log holds it, and the answer to this call is a reference and nothing else.

Run it

python samples/change_password.py <terminal id> --key-id mfxk_... --private-key-file <your key file>

Your key needs the scopes term:read and term:write. The login, the server and the new password are typed at a prompt and go nowhere else. The script prints each change of state and ends with PASS when the terminal is ACTIVE on the new password.

The runnable sample: samples/change_password.py

Executed in CI against MFX Hub on every change to the knowledge base.

"""Change a terminal's broker password: submit the new one, and watch the terminal log in with it.

The runnable half of guides/changing-a-terminals-password.md. It does only what a customer can do:
every call is the public, signed API through the SDK.

    python samples/change_password.py <terminal id> --key-id mfxk_... --private-key-file <your key file>

The login, the server and the new password are typed at a prompt. They are never an argument, an
environment variable or a file, so they reach no shell history, no process list and no CI log.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import os
import asyncio
import getpass
import time
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from mfx import MfxApiError, MfxClient, Secret, SigningKey

BASE_URL = "https://api.dev.mfxhub.com/v1"
POLL_S = 5
#: A restart or a fresh login is usually under two minutes; a cold host can take longer.
TIMEOUT_S = 20 * 60
#: How long a restart has to show itself before a live terminal is taken as already restarted.
RESTART_SEEN_S = 120
#: What shows a terminal is logged in. Ticks are not part of it: a terminal with no instruments,
#: or one whose market is closed, is logged in and quotes nothing.
LIVE = ("ProcessRunning", "BrokerConnected")

def private_key(args: argparse.Namespace) -> str:
    """The API private key: the file named by --private-key-file, else MFX_PRIVATE_KEY."""
    if args.private_key_file is not None:
        return str(args.private_key_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
    key = os.environ.get("MFX_PRIVATE_KEY")
    if not key:
        raise SystemExit("give --private-key-file, or set MFX_PRIVATE_KEY")
    return key.strip()



def field(answer: Any, name: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
    """A field of the answer, whether or not this SDK version has a typed attribute for it."""
    data = answer.to_dict() if hasattr(answer, "to_dict") else dict(answer)
    return data.get(name, default)


async def change_password(
    client: MfxClient, terminal_id: str, *, login: int, server: str, password: Secret
) -> Any:
    """Submit the same login with its new password. The second submission is the rotation."""
    try:
        return await client.terminals.submit_credentials(
            terminal_id,
            login=login,
            password=password,
            server=server,
            idempotency_key=f"change-password-{uuid.uuid4()}",
        )
    except MfxApiError as refused:
        # 409 conflict: another login is another account, so it needs its own terminal.
        # 409 state_error: the terminal is draining or retired.
        raise SystemExit(f"REFUSED: {refused}") from refused


def live(terminal: Any) -> bool:
    """ACTIVE with the process up and the broker connected."""
    if str(terminal.state) != "ACTIVE":
        return False
    seen = terminal.conditions.to_dict() if terminal.conditions else {}
    return all(seen.get(name, {}).get("status") == "ok" for name in LIVE)


async def wait_until_live(client: MfxClient, terminal_id: str, *, restarting: bool) -> str:
    """Poll until the terminal is live on the new password, printing each change.

    A restart keeps the terminal `ACTIVE` while its host stops and starts it, so the state alone
    cannot show it finished. `restarting` waits to see it stop being live first, for up to
    `RESTART_SEEN_S`; a restart quicker than the poll is taken as done.
    """
    started = time.monotonic()
    last = None
    seen_down = not restarting
    while time.monotonic() - started < TIMEOUT_S:
        terminal = await client.terminals.get(terminal_id)
        now_live = live(terminal)
        shown = (str(terminal.state), now_live)
        if shown != last:
            print(f"[{int(time.monotonic() - started):>4}s] {shown[0]} live={now_live}")
            last = shown
        if str(terminal.state) in ("FAILED", "RETIRED"):
            return str(terminal.state)
        seen_down = seen_down or not now_live or time.monotonic() - started > RESTART_SEEN_S
        if now_live and seen_down:
            return "ACTIVE"
        await asyncio.sleep(POLL_S)
    raise SystemExit(f"FAILED: not live after {TIMEOUT_S}s")


async def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    parser.add_argument("terminal_id")
    parser.add_argument("--key-id", default=os.environ.get("MFX_KEY_ID"), help="or MFX_KEY_ID")
    parser.add_argument("--private-key-file", type=Path, help="or the key itself in MFX_PRIVATE_KEY")
    parser.add_argument("--base-url", default=BASE_URL)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    client = MfxClient(
        args.base_url, args.key_id, SigningKey(private_key(args))
    )
    before = await client.terminals.get(args.terminal_id)
    print(f"terminal {args.terminal_id} is {before.state}")

    login = int(input("Broker login (the one this terminal already has): "))
    server = input("Broker server: ").strip()
    password = Secret(getpass.getpass("New password: "))

    answer = await change_password(
        client, args.terminal_id, login=login, server=server, password=password
    )
    takes_effect = field(answer, "takes_effect", "first_login")
    print(f"accepted: rotated={field(answer, 'rotated', False)} takes_effect={takes_effect}")

    if takes_effect == "next_login":
        why = field(answer, "not_applied_reason")
        print("Stored. The terminal uses the new password the next time it logs in.")
        if why:
            print(f"It was not restarted now: {why}")
        return
    state = await wait_until_live(client, args.terminal_id, restarting=takes_effect == "restart")
    print("PASS" if state == "ACTIVE" else f"FAILED: the terminal is {state}; read its conditions")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

A restart keeps the terminal `ACTIVE` while its host stops and starts it, so the state alone cannot show it finished. `restarting` waits to see it stop being live first, for up to `RESTART_SEEN_S`; a restart quicker than the poll is taken as done. """ started = time.monotonic() last = None seen_down = not restarting while time.monotonic() - started < TIMEOUT_S: terminal = await client.terminals.get(terminal_id) now_live = live(terminal) shown = (str(terminal.state), now_live) if shown != last: print(f"[{int(time.monotonic() - started):>4}s] {shown[0]} live={now_live}") last = shown if str(terminal.state) in ("FAILED", "RETIRED"): return str(terminal.state) seen_down = seen_down or not now_live or time.monotonic() - started > RESTART_SEEN_S if now_live and seen_down: return "ACTIVE" await asyncio.sleep(POLL_S) raise SystemExit(f"FAILED: not live after {TIMEOUT_S}s") async def main() -> None: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0]) parser.add_argument("terminal_id") parser.add_argument("--key-id", default=os.environ.get("MFX_KEY_ID"), help="or MFX_KEY_ID") parser.add_argument("--private-key-file", type=Path, help="or the key itself in MFX_PRIVATE_KEY") parser.add_argument("--base-url", default=BASE_URL) args = parser.parse_args() client = MfxClient( args.base_url, args.key_id, SigningKey(private_key(args)) ) before = await client.terminals.get(args.terminal_id) print(f"terminal {args.terminal_id} is {before.state}") login = int(input("Broker login (the one this terminal already has): ")) server = input("Broker server: ").strip() password = Secret(getpass.getpass("New password: ")) answer = await change_password( client, args.terminal_id, login=login, server=server, password=password ) takes_effect = field(answer, "takes_effect", "first_login") print(f"accepted: rotated={field(answer, 'rotated', False)} takes_effect={takes_effect}") if takes_effect == "next_login": why = field(answer, "not_applied_reason") print("Stored. The terminal uses the new password the next time it logs in.") if why: print(f"It was not restarted now: {why}") return state = await wait_until_live(client, args.terminal_id, restarting=takes_effect == "restart") print("PASS" if state == "ACTIVE" else f"FAILED: the terminal is {state}; read its conditions") if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main())

Your users want to see their balance, equity, margin and every open position's floating profit move as the market moves. MFX pushes that to you over the stream. This guide explains what arrives, how to keep your copy correct, and how to do it for thousands of users without wasting bandwidth.

Two kinds of thing arrive

Kind Examples Channel After a reconnect
The account as it is now balance, equity, margin, free margin, margin level, the open positions with their current price and floating profit account:{terminal_id}, one per terminal you get the current state again
Things that happened a position opened, modified or closed; the account's profile changed events missed ones are replayed for up to 15 minutes
Your orders' outcomes filled, rejected, expired results:{terminal_id} missed ones are replayed for up to 15 minutes

The account is state: only the latest version matters, so MFX never replays old versions to you. Events and order outcomes are history: none may be lost, so MFX replays what you missed. Keep the two apart in your own code too.

Subscribing to an account

Open the stream, then subscribe to account:{terminal_id} for each terminal you want to follow. Your key needs the scope acct:read, and the terminal must be yours.

You receive two kinds of message on that channel:

Message When What it carries
account.snapshot as soon as you subscribe; again whenever a position opens, closes or changes (stop loss, take profit, volume); and every 60 seconds everything: the account figures, every open position in full, the pending orders, and as_of
account.marks in between, whenever prices move, at the terminal's refresh rate; every 5 seconds even if nothing moved the account figures, and for each position whose price or profit moved: its ticket, current price, floating profit and swap

A snapshot is the whole picture. A marks message is a small update to the snapshot you already hold. For an account with a few positions, a marks message is a few hundred bytes; for an account with hundreds of positions, it is still a small fraction of a snapshot.

Every message carries a seq, which increases on that channel, and a base: the seq of the snapshot it applies to. A snapshot's base is its own seq.

Amounts are decimal strings ("10012.40"), never floating-point numbers. Parse them as decimals.

Keeping your copy correct

Four rules. The SDK's live account view follows them for you; if you use the raw stream, follow them yourself.

  1. Replace on a snapshot. Throw away your copy and take the snapshot as it is.
  2. Apply marks only to the snapshot they name. If a marks message's base is the seq of the snapshot you hold, update the account figures and, for each ticket in it, the position's current price, floating profit and swap. If its base is different, or it names a ticket you do not have, your copy is behind: ignore it. The next snapshot arrives within 60 seconds, or ask for one now with resume.
  3. On a gap in seq, send resume. On this channel the answer is a fresh snapshot, never a replay of old messages.
  4. Use the events for what happened, the snapshot for what is. Show a notification when position.opened or position.closed arrives on events; draw the list of positions from the snapshot and its marks.

If nothing at all arrives on an account channel for 15 seconds while the account has open positions, treat the numbers as stale and say so. GET /v1/terminals/{id}/account answers the same picture with a stale flag.

Doing it for thousands of users

These practices matter most when one platform serves many users, each with their own terminal.

  • Keep a channel subscribed for as long as you need it. An account channel may stay subscribed around the clock: that is the supported way to watch equity for a risk rule, such as a daily-loss limit, while nobody is looking. Channels ride your connections, and your plan limits how many connections you hold (ws_conns in GET /v1/usage), so carry many accounts on a few connections. Where nothing needs an account's live figures, such as a screen nobody has open, unsubscribe: fewer channels mean fewer messages for you to process.
  • Use a few connections, not one per user. One stream connection carries many channels. Multiplex your users' subscriptions over a small pool of connections from your servers, and fan the updates out to your users yourself.
  • Do not poll. Everything on the account arrives on the stream. Read the REST endpoints for a page that is not live, such as an account statement, or to check one value; never call them in a loop.
  • Choose each terminal's refresh rate on purpose. It sets how often prices are swept and how often the account's marks can arrive. One second is plenty for a display. A faster rate means more messages and uses more of your plan's capacity, so keep it for users who need it.
  • Keep marks cheap on your side. A marks message is designed to be applied in place: look up the ticket, set three numbers. Avoid rebuilding a whole page or writing every message to a database.
  • Store what you need from events, not from marks. If you keep history, write position.* events and your order outcomes. The marks stream is a live view, not a record.

Reconnecting

The stream connection has a maximum lifetime of 24 hours, and networks drop. After reconnecting:

  • for each account channel you had, subscribe again (or resume): you get the current snapshot;
  • for events and results:{terminal_id}, resume with the last seq you saw: you get what you missed from the last 15 minutes, or resync if it was longer, in which case read the current state over REST.

Run it

The sample follows one terminal's account live, applies marks to the snapshot it holds, and prints every update with the time since it started:

python samples/account_live.py --key-id mfxk_... --private-key-file <your key file> --terminal <terminal id>

Your key needs the scope acct:read.
